change.describe: branch `pr-37634` of keycloak-37634 against c22f76867f595f0f7c327376a66a08dca01949e8 (merge-base c22f768)
change.title: pr-37634
change.description:
Encoding context to access token IDs closes #37118
Shorter encoding of access token
change.author: mposolda

findings.title: isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut: wrong offset and inverted condition
findings.body: The encoded prefix is `<session 2><tokenType 2><grant 2>` (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114-117), so the grant shortcut is `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. For `onrtac` the code reads `ta`, which never equals any grant shortcut. The condition is also inverted: it returns `false` when the shortcut *matches*. Together these mean the matcher accepts any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` whatever the grant, so `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` never check the grant type, which is the thing this PR adds. If you fix only the offset, every correct token fails instead. Suggested fix: `if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check tests grantType instead
findings.body: Line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`, which checks `grantType` a second time. A null `rawTokenId` gets through, and `encodeTokenId` (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:117) then produces an id like `onrtac:null` without any error. It should be `requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: Client credentials (and UMA, legacy token exchange) tokens are encoded with grant 'na', so 'cc'/'pg' are never written
findings.body: The grant type attribute is only set in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` (auth code, device, CIBA), the ROPC grant, refresh, pre-authorized code and `StandardTokenExchangeProvider`. `ClientCredentialsGrantType` builds its token via `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` (ClientCredentialsGrantType.java:140) and never sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`. So `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` falls back to `UNKNOWN` (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:57-60), and every client-credentials access token gets the id `trrtna:...`/`onrtna:...` instead of `..cc:...`. The same gap exists for `AuthorizationTokenService.java:357` (UMA `pg`) and the V1 `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:409`. Nothing errors, but the encoded context is wrong for these grants, which defeats the feature for its most common machine-to-machine case. Set `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` before generating the token in these paths, and add an AssertEvents expectation for client credentials.

findings.title: Javadoc says '3-letters' shortcut, but the decoder requires exactly 2 characters and nothing checks the length
findings.body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects any prefix that is not 6 characters long (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-76) and reads the grant as `substring(4, 6)`. A custom grant that follows this javadoc and returns a 3-letter shortcut gets encoded without error by `encodeTokenId`, but its ids then fail to decode. Say "exactly 2 characters" in the javadoc and validate the length (and non-null) in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`. A null shortcut currently throws an NPE from `ConcurrentHashMap.put` at startup with no useful message. A third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` compiled before this change has no `getShortcut()` at all, so it hits `AbstractMethodError` in `postInit`. A default method, or a clear error, would make that failure easier to understand.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes on a NullPointerException, not the intended validation
findings.body: The factory is built without `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` is null. For the unknown shortcut `ac`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` falls into the refresh branch and calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:125), which throws an NPE. Because the test catches the broad `RuntimeException`, it passes because of that NPE and never reaches the `IllegalArgumentException` at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:93. Mock or stub the session factory and catch `IllegalArgumentException`.

contracts.action: initToken now derives the access token id from the TokenContextEncoderProvider instead of a raw UUID
contracts.equivalent_path: Grant paths that set Constants.GRANT_TYPE before token creation: OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, ROPC, refresh, pre-authorized code, standard token exchange
contracts.before_after: Client credentials, UMA and V1 token exchange build tokens through responseBuilder without setting the attribute, so they encode 'na'
contracts.visible_effect: The jti / TOKEN_ID event detail becomes '<ss><tt><gg>:<uuid>'; client-credentials tokens show 'na' as the grant
contracts.failure_mode: encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException if the grant type is not registered; grant_type is resolved to a registered factory by TokenEndpoint, so in practice an unset value falls back to 'na'

contracts.action: Lightweight token detection made public static and called from the encoder
contracts.equivalent_path: AllowedWebOriginsProtocolMapper / AudienceResolveProtocolMapper call getShouldUseLightweightToken during mapper transform
contracts.before_after: The encoder reads the same client attribute and session attribute (set by UseLightweightAccessTokenExecutor on client policy events) earlier, in initToken
contracts.visible_effect: The token type shortcut 'lt'/'rt' in the jti

summary: The encoder SPI is wired in correctly, but a few things need fixing. The new AssertEvents matcher reads the wrong characters and has its condition inverted, so it never checks the grant type. AccessTokenContext checks grantType for null twice and never checks rawTokenId. Client credentials, UMA and V1 token exchange tokens never set the grant type attribute, so their ids encode 'na'. The shortcut javadoc says 3 letters while the decoder requires exactly 2, and the unit test for an incorrect grant type passes on a NullPointerException.
